## NEW #1 DETAIL — AWS Agent Registry GA + ORGANIZATION-WIDE AUTO-DETECTION
Doc: .../devguide/registry-organizations.html
- Auto-detects `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime` and `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Gateway` across ALL
  AWS Organizations MEMBER ACCOUNTS into one ORGANIZATION-SCOPED REGISTRY.
- "Fully managed. ... NO AGENTS, NO PER-ACCOUNT PERMISSIONS, and no member-account resources to set up."
- ONE org-scoped registry PER REGION. Owned by mgmt account or (AWS-recommended) a DELEGATED ADMIN.
  Requires organizations:EnableAWSServiceAccess + RegisterDelegatedAdministrator, and the SLR
  AWSServiceRoleForAgentRegistry in the MANAGEMENT account (and in the admin account too if CMK).
- Initial discovery of pre-existing resources takes UP TO 20 MINUTES.
- Record name: `aws-autodetected-<accountId>-<region>-<resourceId>` (NOT the display name).
- provenance[]: relation DETECTED_FROM, sourceId = source ARN, sourceType = the CFN type.
  sourceDetails carries JWT `discoveryUrl` and `workloadIdentityArn`.

## KEY RULES — NEW THIS SCAN (all four are detection content)
- CANNOT DISTINGUISH MCP SERVER FROM AGENT. Every runtime protocol (MCP, HTTP, A2A, AGUI) maps to
  recordType=AGENT, "because auto-detection can't distinguish a standalone MCP server from an agent
  that exposes an MCP interface." You may hand-narrow AGENT->MCP, but a later PROTOCOL CHANGE
  RESETS IT BACK TO AGENT and overrides your narrowing. Gateway records are always GATEWAY.
- AUTHORIZER DETAIL IS TRUNCATED. `AllowedClients`, `AllowedAudience`, `AllowedScopes` are
  **NOT carried into the record** — only discoveryUrl is. => the registry CANNOT answer
  "who may call this agent". Must read the source resource.
- DEPRECATION SILENTLY FREEZES SYNC. "If you deprecate an auto-detected record ... auto-detection
  stops syncing changes from the source resource ... Subsequent updates — such as protocol,
  authorizer, or endpoint changes — are NOT applied." => plausible evasion path.
- TWO STATUS FIELDS, AND THEY DISAGREE. `autoDetectionConfiguration.enabled` (what you request) vs
  `autoDetection.status` ACTIVE/INACTIVE (what is in effect). enabled=true is NECESSARY BUT NOT
  SUFFICIENT. => enabled=true + status=INACTIVE means the org believes discovery runs and it does not.
  AWS also flips enabled to false itself when trusted access is disabled or the delegated admin is
  deregistered — and RE-ENABLING TRUSTED ACCESS DOES NOT RESUME AUTO-DETECTION.
- Auto-detected records CANNOT BE DELETED while auto-detection is enabled.
- A refresh of an APPROVED record is written as a NEW DRAFT REVISION, undiscoverable until approved;
  the old approved revision stays discoverable meanwhile => discoverable view can lag reality.
- Field ownership split: you own name/description/recordVersion/descriptor data; the service owns
  descriptor protocol, descriptor source URL, and provenance (edits rejected).

## NEW #2 DETAIL — Memory IngestData
Doc: .../devguide/long-term-ingest-data.html ; API_IngestData.html
"Submit content directly for long-term memory extraction, WITHOUT persisting it as a short-term
 memory event." => "the submitted content CANNOT BE RETRIEVED with GetEvent, ListEvents, or
 ListSessions, or reorganized with branching."
Payload types: `conversational` (role USER/ASSISTANT + text) and `json` (behavioral events, activity
 logs, system events). Optional structured metadata. Scoped by actorId + sessionId + namespace;
 content sharing all three "is treated as related context during extraction."
FANS OUT to EVERY configured long-term strategy EXCEPT self-managed ones.
Async. Failures -> dedicated queue; ListMemoryExtractionJobs / StartMemoryExtractionJob to re-drive;
 FailedExtraction CloudWatch metric. Kinesis memory-record streaming gives real-time create notices.
>>> PROGRESSION: 08-23 = memory write no longer needs a CONVERSATION (json on CreateEvent).
>>> 09-02 = memory write no longer needs an EVENT. Only CloudTrail / Kinesis remain as signals.

## NEW #4 DETAIL — Agent Registry PrivateLink
TWO interface endpoints:
  com.amazonaws.<region>.agent-registry-control  — registry and record MANAGEMENT
  com.amazonaws.<region>.agent-registry          — record DISCOVERY + THE REGISTRY MCP ENDPOINT
Endpoint policies match callers by IAM principal. FOR JWT-AUTHORIZED REGISTRIES YOU MUST SET
`Principal` TO `*` so bearer-token requests can reach the service. => the VPC endpoint policy on a
JWT registry is wide open by design; authorization lives entirely in the JWT.

## KEY RULES CARRIED FORWARD (unchanged)
- RAM org-internal shares AUTO-ACCEPT (no consumer consent event). Revocation ~30 s eventually
  consistent. AWSRAMPermissionAgentRegistryForConsumer (AWS's recommended default) includes
  agent-registry:InvokeRegistryMcp => the share is a LIVE TOOL-INVOCATION GRANT.
  Condition keys RecordCreatorAccount / RecordSourceAccount are NOT evaluated on Create or on
  Search/List => a scoped consumer can still enumerate the WHOLE catalogue.
- Memory extraction asymmetry: conversational + JSON are extracted to long-term; BLOB payloads are
  short-term only and NOT extracted. Payload TYPE decides influence on future sessions.
- x402 `upto` pays a metered amount up to a ceiling via Permit2; MPP forwards a
  `WWW-Authenticate: Payment` challenge VERBATIM to ProcessPayment.
- Third-party evaluators are discoverable via ListEvaluators ALONGSIDE built-in and custom —
  provenance NOT distinguished on the inventory surface.

## July 2026 and earlier — unchanged from the 2026-08-26 capture.

namespace, control/data-plane APIs, MCP endpoint and PrivateLink endpoints. RECOMMEND adding
